correctness.rationale: The proposed square-contact scheme is explicitly defined as the vanishing locus of two odd mixed coefficients; in characteristic two a degree-four binary form is a polynomial square iff both are zero. Lines at dual infinity W=0 cannot enter because the odd coefficient c (when V nonzero) or the coefficient 1 (line X=0) is a unit, scheme-theoretically. In the W=1 chart Z=uX+vY, independent symbolic expansion modulo 2 confirmed odd coefficients v(a+c u²), u+c v³. Eliminating u=c v³ gives av+c³v^7, and since c is invertible the normalized monic relation v^7+(a/c³)v gives a free family basis {1,v,...,v^6}; finite flatness holds over the smooth coefficient base. In a nonzero-a geometric fibre v(v³+s)², s²=a/c³, and the cubic has simple roots since its derivative v² is nonzero at roots, yielding local lengths 1,2,2,2; when a=0 the quotient is k[v]/v^7 and the maximal ideal has Hilbert function seven ones. Smoothness follows since f and f prime have no common root in affine chart, and the point at infinity has nonzero Z derivative. This statement is only about the particular square-contact scheme, not theta-characteristic moduli or mixed characteristic.

value.rationale: Geometric bitangent support counts of characteristic-two genus-three quartics do not determine infinitesimal multiplicity or flat specialization. An explicit finite flat rank-seven incidence scheme on a natural Picard subfamily, including a curvilinear length-seven collision and full Hilbert function, gives independently useful local geometry beyond the known 4-point and 1-point supports. Its definition is motivated by square-contact lines rather than an arbitrary numerical invariant.
